title: Create a "Cohort Icebreaker" Content Pack
description: To drive engagement, bootcamps need activities. Write a set of structured prompts that a bootcamp instructor can post in a Zedu channel on Day 1 to get students talking and using the platform features correctly.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Add low-disclosure and asynchronous alternatives to each prompt
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Review the ten day-one prompts and add a voluntary low-disclosure option plus an asynchronous way to participate for each, without changing the feature-learning goal. Flag prompts that ask for personal details, add a facilitator note for learners who prefer to observe first, and check that each alternative still practices the intended Zedu feature. Deliver a prompt-to-alternative table, copy-ready variants, and mobile/accessibility checks. This complements the existing prompt pack rather than creating another set of ten.

Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Pair each prompt with the instructor's follow-up reply and a moderation note
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A prompt only works if the instructor keeps it going. For each day-one prompt, add a short model reply the instructor posts after the first answers (to show the expected tone and model the feature being taught), a nudge for quiet learners, and a moderation note on what to do if a reply oversteps, for example personal details or off-topic arguments. Done: the ten prompts each with reply, nudge and moderation note, in a copy-paste format ready for a Zedu channel.

upvotes.reason: "Pair each prompt with the instructor's follow-up reply and a moderation note" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

Instructor follow-up examples and privacy-aware moderation notes make the existing icebreakers easier to run responsibly; nudges should remain optional and avoid pressuring learners to disclose personal information.

This is a practical extension to the approved ten-prompt pack: instructor replies and nudges help the activity continue, while a moderation note helps facilitators handle personal details or off-topic replies. It stays tied to the existing prompts instead of duplicating them.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Ten day-one prompts that teach Zedu channel features by using them
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Create a pack of ten icebreaker prompts an instructor can post in a Zedu channel on day one. Each prompt should get students to use one platform feature correctly (thread reply, file upload, mention, reaction, pinned answer) while answering a simple getting-to-know-you question. Include a facilitator note, timing, and a copy-paste version for each prompt. One task: write the pack and check every feature against the live site.
